messages:
sam: Escalation from ACME — after last runtime deploy we're seeing p99 regressions on streaming TTFB. Customer says initial chunk is often 900ms-1.5s. Non-streaming total time is ~1.1s so app UX looks bad because TTFB spikes but end-to-end is similar. Request id: req-acme-98765. Link to trace: https://internal.traces/req-acme-98765 :eyes:

jess: Ack. Can you paste the exact curl + headers you used to repro? Also which edge (region/isp) is their traffic coming from?

sam: Repro steps I gave customer:
```
curl -v -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" \
  -H "User-Agent: ACME-client/1.2" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-lite","prompt":"hello","stream":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.com/v1/outputs/stream
```
Headers we see in inbound logs: x-forwarded-for via us-west-2 edge, client path = Akamai -> our edge -> runtime. They also tried HTTP/2 multiplexed client.

maria: Customer notes it happens mostly during cold periods and when concurrency >200. They said switching to non-stream endpoint (sync) removes the TTFB spike.

kai: Looks like classic initial-chunk interleaving / coalescing problem on the edge proxy. If the runtime emits the first token quickly but the proxy buffers to reach a flush threshold we can see inflated TTFB while total is unchanged. Two quick asks: can we get an example response header set and the raw chunk timing from the runtime? (x-runtime-first-chunk-ms, x-batch-size, x-proxy-flush)

sam: From logs for req-acme-98765:
```
x-runtime-first-chunk-ms: 85
x-batch-size: 1
x-proxy-flush-window-ms: 250
x-edge-node: us-west-2-edge-14
x-conn-proto: h2
```

kai: That flush-window looks suspicious (250ms). Recent edge deploy bumped coalescing window for h2 to reduce small-packet overhead. That explains cold-path p99 TTFB but not total. Two mitigation options: 1) quick mitigation — set the customer's route to non-streaming or force chunk-flush (stream_flush_interval=20ms) on edge for their tenant; 2) longer fix — revert the coalescing change or make it adaptive based on initial-chunk-latency telemetry.

alex: I see a deploy at ts 4412340000 that changed h2 coalescing defaults. Rolling that back could be a quick way to test. Will prepare a rollback candidate.

jess: For customer-facing workaround can we proxy their tenant to non-stream for now? That will increase p99 tokens but preserve UX. Need legal/contract check? It's a config change only.

sam: I'll ask ACME if they can toggle to non-stream for a test window. Also asked them to re-run curl with `--no-http2` to see if it's h2-specific.

maria: Customer tried --no-http2 and reported TTFB dropped to ~120ms. So h2 path + edge coalescing combo is the root cause. They are OK with a temporary non-stream workaround.

kai: Notes for devs: create a small feature flag to disable h2 coalescing per-tenant or lower flush-window for streaming responses that have first-chunk latency < 200ms. I'll open a ticket with perf numbers and a proposed rollout.

alex: Ops action: staging rollback test queued. If it reproduces, we can perform canary rollback on us-west-2-edge nodes.

ops-bot: Incident tag added: streaming-ttfb-h2-coalesce-4412345678, severity: low -> medium. Assigned: kai, alex. :hammer_and_wrench: 

sam: TL;DR for ACME: root cause = edge h2 coalescing introduced in recent deploy. Workarounds: (A) switch their route to non-stream (temporary) (B) have them use HTTP/1.1 (--no-http2) (C) we can canary rollback edge change. Customer prefers (A) for now.

kai: Follow-ups: ticket #INF-2389, include telemetry query to detect other tenants affected (look for runtime-first-chunk << proxy-flush-window and high p99 TTFB). Also add a dashboard alert.

sam: Thanks — sharing this with the customer now. Will update when they confirm the non-stream toggle. :thumbsup:
